For as long as I could remember, I could see her in my dreams. The sparkle of her flawness skin, the softness beneath her gentle expression, and the silky texture of her long, dark hair. Every night, I would see her without fail. As I grew up, so did she. We got to watch each other mature from being boisterous kids into mature adults. Though we only knew each other from my dreams, we innately knew that this wasn't a dream; it was real. And it was real for twenty-two years, when I had my first nightmare, and then my first true dream.

I still remember the last time I saw her. She had been acting different for the past few months, talking about there being others even though I had never seen another person, let alone thing for as long as I've known her. We were always stuck in a bright, featureless, white room. The only things that changed was us. By the last days, her soft demeanor was serving merely as a shield to mask her terror. I couldn't fathom what she could be scared of, but that was because I couldn't fathom at all. She had tried to help me see the world that existed; the one that she was always able to see, but because I was an idiot it looked featureless and empty. It wasn't until the last day that I finally was able to capture a brief glimpse of the world that she saw: a failed world. It was as if the universe had had an abortion, with the way that the geometries folded in on themselves. And it was on this absolutely alien world that I saw the deepest parts of her humanity scattered, her smile literally flying for miles.

The next night was the worst. I wondered if I would see her. Instead I had my first normal dream -- if normal could even be applied here. It felt so incredibly weird and painful, that even in this truest of dreams that even my subconsciousness knew that this was wrong. It took me a few days to come to terms that I had witnessed her die in a world that is barely fathomable, and by forces or creatures that are nightmarishly indescribable. I can't even say that I saw them, only the damage they inflicted upon her. The more I tried to process what happened, I came to realize just how truly unfathomable the entire thing was: Who was she? Why was there a human in this alien world? How did she survive there for so long, let alone survive there period? Where is this place? Why was I able to join in with her? Why wasn't I hurt or attacked? So many questions flooded my mind, that I knew that I had to get answers.

The answer to these questions lied in entropy. Every movement, every firing synapse, and every biochemical reaction added to the natural entropy of the world. Through carefully documenting specific details, and doing so before my own memories ultimately failed me, an entropic profile could be built. The physical sciences could give me the groundwork of what I was searching for, but the magical sciences could give me the resources to find the needle in the hay stack.

When magic was imported to our universe nearly a century ago, it sparked a new revolution of how to see the world. Whereas physics could be said to be the software of the universe, magic instead was the bits on the hard drive. Flip a bit, and you could change the world. Or alternatively, you could search for specific sequences of bits. It only took two years and countless sleepless nights when I finally ran the search program for the first time, and only a few seconds later when it spat out the answer. I trembled in excitement; my sweaty hands shaking the keys on the keyboard.

Eureka! I had found her! I didn't know where she was specifically since that was outside the domain of the magic, but based on the data readings it was suggestive of being inside the event horizon of a black hole. She lived in a pocket dimension of our own, and somehow we were linked. Though why? And still, who was she? All questions that would be answered in due time. Now that I knew the coordinates of the data, I had the computer rebuild her data profile. By following the entropic profile that it found, it could work forward and backwards to read the entire profile. Every movement, firing synapse, and biochemical reaction of hers would be known. Combine the data with teleporter technology, and I could rebuild her. I left the program running overnight to finish the process. By the time I returned to the lab early in the morning, she would hopefully be there.

Instead I awoke at 2AM with a splitting headache. A pulsating hotness permeated my entire body, leaving me weak. It took a good few minutes for me to even be able to physically get up, with a few times me finding myself hugging the floor as the world seemed to spin around me. A deep suspicion of bad omens rises up from my gut and coats the hardwood floor. My body refuses to tremble even as I gather the synaptic courage to finally stand and get myself ready. I can feel it in my blood that she is alive.

Even though the lab is only two floors down from my sleeping quarters, it still feels like I had to jog a marathon just to get there. All along the way the familiar world seems to ripple and wave. The straight corridors that criss-cross my building now weave and bend in unusual patterns. Textures and colors are thrown off. I rub my eyes, hoping that maybe I am still tired, but it is to no avail. I contemplate for a moment if this might simply be a dream, but I rule that option out. Finally at the destination, I open the door.

The monitor greets me with a "Process completed..." output, along with some various data about the operation. As I start to look around the room, my eyes jerk back to the screen for a moment to read a number: 27.889Gy. The total size of the entropic signature as measured in years. It's longer than the life of the universe. I blink my eyes hoping that maybe it's just a haze in my eyes that is fudging the numbers, but that is the output. It is undeniable: I have just reborn a person who is older than the universe itself. Just as it starts clicking that I should probably look for her, she finds me instead.

An exceptionally violent headache sends me crashing to the floor in front of the computer. My muscles spasm painfully. I want to cry out in pain, but even my diaphragm is paralyzed in spasms. As my consciousness begins to fade, I see a shadow move across the wall in front of me. I want to say I could hear anything, but a loud ringing is all that my ears pick up. Quickly the shadow expands and envelops my entire field of vision, and then I see white.

Once again, I stand in the featureless white box, with her standing nearby. Though I had aged two years since we last met, she was just as I remembered her from two years ago. I had succeeded in bringing her back from the dead, but now I have to question if that was such a good idea. That was quickly proven to be a moot point, as she grabbed me and forcibly started french kissing me. I could have resisted, and I probably should have resisted, but I felt at peace in her presence. Less peaceful was when she sealed my lips with hers, and started vomiting herself into my body. There is no way to describe what raw information tastes like, but the texture is like that of a pureed silk scarf mixed with the diarrhea of a homeless person whose diet consisted of sand and cardboard. My body shuddered, and kept shuddering even after she was gone. But as she was gone, so was I. We were now one, forever trapped inside the bright box.

In physics, every particle has an anti-particle. Through quantum processes, the particles can even be linked through entanglement. In magic, a similar phenomena can happen with souls. My soul and hers functioned opposites to each other, and as such linked. And when in close proximity to each other, our souls simply dissolved the boundaries separating each other and fused. Thus the question of who she is became the same as asking who I am. So now I stand alone, forever, waiting for countless years until another soul will entangle with mine so I may briefly have company once more.
